EEG measurements have been widely applied in clinical settings to diagnose and study disorders such as epilepsy
(Smith, 2005; Acharya et al., 2013; Noachtar & Remi ´ , 2009; Tan et al., 2025) and multiple
sclerosis (Mouazen et al., 2025; Striano et al., 2003). EEG analysis can also be used to determine the stages
of sleep (Supratak et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2024b; Li et al., 2022), diagnose sleep disorders (Tiwari et al.,
2022), and have been the basis of our understanding of various fundamental brain rhythms such as alpha, beta,
gamma, and theta waves within the brain (Buzsaki, 2006).

Researchers have successfully decoded global brainstates such as focus (Su et al., 2022; Al-Nafjan & Aldayel,
2022; Kaushik et al., 2022), emotions (Liang et al., 2019; Duan et al., 2020), meditative states (Schoenberg &
Vago, 2019; Kora et al., 2021; Faber et al., 2017), stages of sleep (Supratak et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2024b;
Li et al., 2022) and many more from EEG data using relatively simple methods.

The key intuition is that learning to denoise at all noise levels teaches the model a vector field that points
back toward high-density regions of pdata. In the continuous-time limit this connects to score-based modeling
(Hyvarinen & Dayan ¨ , 2005; Vincent, 2011), where the network approximates the score function and sampling
follows a learned reverse diffusion trajectory.
